A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Doppelgangers++ work, with readable and matchable text, equations, tables, and figures. All supplied pages were inspected. Neither PDF contains an appendix; both refer to separate supplementary material that is not included.

before.justification: V1 reports original pairwise classification and SfM reconstruction experiments in Tables 1–2, qualitative reconstruction results, and model ablations in Section 4.5 and Figure 8.

after.justification: V2 retains these original classification, reconstruction, and ablation results. Their retention from v1 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The mining rules, frozen MASt3R backbone, multi-level features, two Transformer classification heads, symmetrized inputs, cross-entropy training, test-time voting, and SfM filtering procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on DG and VisymScenes, evaluate classification on DG, VisymScenes, and Mapillary, and evaluate reconstruction on the same 16 existing scenes and five VisymScenes scenes.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain DG-OG for classification, COLMAP and DG-OG in Table 2, and MASt3R-SfM in the qualitative comparison. V2's new Baselines paragraph mentions additional prior methods but provides no new experimental comparisons against them.

E3.justification: The data splits, sample counts, model configuration, training budget, classification metrics, reconstruction evaluation, and pruning thresholds are unchanged. The added baseline-selection explanation does not revise an evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Figure 8 retain the same four ablations: backbone fine-tuning, one versus two heads, MLP versus Transformer heads, and final-layer versus multi-layer features. The cross-domain evaluations and reconstruction case studies are also retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and precision-recall curves without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, uncertainty bands, or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same classification scores, registered-image counts, and inlier ratios. Visual comparison confirms the same ablation curves in Figure 8 and the same qualitative reconstruction findings. The added literature discussion introduces no original result entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–4, including decoder features, classification scores, voting, and aggregated inlier ratio, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: diversified training data, classification using geometric features, improved generalization and SfM reconstruction, and geotag-based reconstruction validation.

C2.justification: The explanations of generalization, head separation, multi-layer features, and possible overfitting remain unchanged. Both versions retain the caution about geotag accuracy and comparing inlier ratios across different scenes.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same architecture and training details, including five epochs, batch size eight, and Adam with learning rate 0.0001. Dataset-mining disclosures and references to supplementary details are unchanged; no new code or data access information appears.

R1.justification: V2 adds 13 distinct cited works, expanding support for the existing discussion of SfM disambiguation and matching. A new Section 4.1 paragraph explains choosing DG-OG through its reported advantages over earlier methods. These additions broaden the context while retaining the same overall research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 adds the short Baselines paragraph, makes small wording edits in Sections 3.3 and 4.1 and the Table 2 caption, and reverses the acknowledgment name order. The section sequence and main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All eight figures and both tables are retained. V2 makes small spacing and caption-layout adjustments, removes page-number footers, and reflows the expanded bibliography onto another page. The displays' scientific content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the scholarly context by acknowledging additional relevant work and explicitly explaining the choice of DG-OG as the primary baseline. This makes the evaluation rationale clearer. The gain is limited: the method, experimental evidence, results, and limitations remain unchanged, and the newly discussed alternatives receive no additional direct evaluation.
